wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: A lamb soup with chickpeas and potatoes in a stone pot; you drink the broth with bread and mash the rest.
Lamb, chickpeas, white beans, potatoes, tomatoes, dried lime, turmeric
Dizi is traditional fare of Tehran's working neighbourhoods, with its own serving ritual.
Patties of minced beef and pork with barberry and spices, wrapped in caul fat and fried.
Beef, pork, caul fat, onion, barberry, garlic, coriander
The name points to Abkhaz origins, but the dish is firmly part of Georgian cuisine.
A thick unsalted cornmeal porridge served instead of bread with cheese and meat.
Abysta is cooked in a cauldron and served with a wooden paddle, often with pieces of cheese pressed into it.
Boiled beans or greens dressed with walnut paste, adjika and herbs.
Green beans or beet greens, walnuts, adjika, coriander
Achapa is the Abkhaz cousin of Georgian pkhali, often made with green beans and beetroot.
Flatbreads of corn or wheat flour filled with young cheese and fried in butter.
Corn or wheat flour, young cheese, butter
Achash is made for breakfast in Abkhaz villages with fresh homemade cheese.
A salad of thinly sliced tomatoes and onion with chilli and herbs, served with plov.
Fresh achichuk balances rich plov, and in Uzbekistan plov is never served without it.
A layered cheese pie: thin sheets of boiled dough are stacked with cheese and butter and baked. In taste and structure it resembles lasagna.
Wheat flour, eggs, sulguni, Imeretian cheese, butter
A dish from Adjara and Abkhazia.
Boiling the dough sheets makes the pie tender inside and crisp on top.
A spicy kebab of hand-minced lamb with red pepper flakes, grilled on a wide skewer over charcoal.
Lamb, tail fat, red pepper flakes, salt
Named after the city of Adana in southern Turkey; the meat is knife-minced and always mixed with tail fat.
Salt ground with garlic and dried herbs: thyme, dill, coriander and pepper.
Salt, garlic, thyme, dill, coriander, red pepper
The Adyghe made this salt to season meat and cheese all year round.
A soft, mild cheese from pasteurised milk with a delicate texture, eaten fresh, fried or smoked.
Adyghe cheese is set with whey rather than rennet; its shape comes from the woven basket it drains in.
A vegetable stew of aubergine, sweet pepper, tomatoes and onion with plenty of herbs and garlic. Served hot or cold.
Aubergine, sweet pepper, tomatoes, onion, garlic, coriander, basil, vegetable oil
Similar vegetable stews are found across the Caucasus.
In Georgia ajapsandali is especially loved in summer when vegetables are ripest.
A hot paste of red pepper, garlic, coriander and salt ground on a stone. Even a spoonful adds heat to a dish.
Hot red pepper, garlic, coriander, blue fenugreek, salt
Adjika means "salt" in Abkhaz; peppers were once ground with salt so it would keep longer.
Thin flatbreads filled with wild greens — nettle, sorrel, orache — and onion.
Wheat flour, water, nettle, sorrel, spring onion, butter
Afarar are baked in spring when the first greens appear in the mountains.
A cornmeal porridge cooked with milk and finished with butter. A simple breakfast dish.
Maize became one of Chechnya's main crops, and porridges made from it are eaten daily.
Small cornmeal cakes baked on a hot pan or in embers.
Akuarchal is the traditional bread of the Abkhaz, served with soups and sauces.
Dried peaches stuffed with crushed walnuts mixed with sugar and cinnamon. A natural, no-bake treat.
The peaches are sun-dried whole after removing the stone.
Such sweets are made in the Ararat Valley.
A clear chicken broth with small chicken meatballs and herbs. A light festive soup.
Chicken, rice, egg, onion, coriander, salt
Arganak was cooked for weddings and holidays in the Ararat Valley.
The broth is simmered long to make it clear.
Homemade egg noodles fried in butter and served with garlic yogurt.
Wheat flour, eggs, butter, matsun yogurt, garlic
Arishta was made in advance: the noodles were dried and kept all winter.
It is cooked in Armenia and Artsakh.
A thick soup with noodles, pulses and herbs, topped with kashk, fried onion and mint.
Reshteh noodles, chickpeas, beans, lentils, spinach, herbs, kashk, onion, mint
Ash reshteh is cooked for Nowruz and to see someone off on a journey; the noodles symbolise the road.
A cold spicy soup with thick noodles, starch jelly, omelette strips and a vinegar dressing.
Wheat noodles, starch jelly, eggs, vinegar, chilli, garlic, herbs
Ashlyan-fu is a Dungan dish that made the town of Karakol on Issyk-Kul famous.
A pudding of wheat, pulses, dried fruit and nuts, cooked in big pots and shared with neighbours.
Wheat, chickpeas, beans, dried apricots, raisins, figs, walnuts, sugar, pomegranate
Legend says Noah made ashure from the last provisions after the Flood; it is cooked in the month of Muharram.
Large pieces of boiled dough served with meat, broth and garlic sauce — not to be confused with Georgian khinkali.
Wheat flour, kefir, baking soda, lamb or beef, garlic, tomato sauce
Khinkal is the main dish of Dagestan; the Avar version has fluffy dough cut into diamonds and cooked in broth.
A refreshing drink of yogurt diluted with cold water, with salt and sometimes mint.
Ayran is drunk throughout the Caucasus and Turkey, and goes especially well with rich meat and kebabs.
Rolls of thin flaky pastry filled with almonds and sugar, dusted with icing sugar.
Wheat flour, butter, eggs, almonds, sugar, cardamom
The name comes from badam, meaning almond.
Badambura is baked in Baku for celebrations.
Thin slices of fried aubergine rolled around a walnut paste with garlic and spices, topped with pomegranate seeds.
Aubergine, walnuts, garlic, coriander, khmeli suneli, wine vinegar, pomegranate
A Georgian feast, the supra, rarely goes without this starter.
A dark home-brewed beer of barley or maize with hops, made for celebrations and rituals.
Barley or maize, hops, water, sugar
In Ossetian the beer is called baegaeny; it is brewed in big pots and served from a shared bowl.
Rice with broad beans and plenty of dill, often served with braised lamb shank.
Rice, broad beans, dill, butter, saffron, lamb shank
A spring dish, made when young broad beans appear.
Dozens of paper-thin pastry layers with pistachios, soaked in syrup — the Turkish take on pakhlava.
Thin pastry, butter, pistachios, sugar, water, lemon juice
Gaziantep pistachio baklava is registered as a protected geographical indication in the EU.
Fish stuffed with walnuts, onion and sour plum paste, baked in an oven or tandoor.
Fish, walnuts, onion, sour plum paste, salt
The fish version of lavangi is made on the Caspian, usually with kutum or carp.
A thick oval flatbread with grooves, sesame and nigella seeds — the classic breakfast bread.
Wheat flour, yeast, water, salt, sesame, nigella seeds
Barbari is eaten in the morning with cheese, herbs and tea; it resembles Armenian matnakash.
Persian ice cream with saffron, rosewater and flakes of frozen cream, sprinkled with pistachios.
Milk, cream, sugar, egg yolks, saffron, rosewater, salep, pistachios
The ice cream is often served between two wafers like a sandwich.
Kebab of beef or lamb marinated in onion and vinegar for a day before grilling.
Beef or lamb, onion, wine vinegar, salt, pepper
The long marinade makes the meat very tender, so bastirma is grilled quickly.
Air-dried beef coated in chaman, a spicy paste of fenugreek, paprika and garlic. Sliced very thin and served as a starter.
Beef tenderloin, salt, fenugreek, paprika, garlic, chilli
Curing meat with spices has long been known in the region.
Wind-drying let people keep meat for months.
Puffy balls or diamonds of yeast dough deep-fried and served with tea.
Wheat flour, yeast, milk, eggs, sugar, vegetable oil
Baursak are fried for celebrations and shared with guests; the round shape symbolises the sun.
A thick walnut sauce with garlic, spices and vinegar. Served with poultry, fish and fried vegetables.
Walnuts, garlic, coriander, blue fenugreek, chilli, wine vinegar, water
Bazhe is the base of many Georgian dishes, including satsivi.
It is especially loved in western Georgia and made for holidays.
Boiled horse meat or lamb on thin squares of dough with onion sauce, served with broth.
Horse meat or lamb, wheat flour, onion, broth
The name means "five fingers", as beshbarmak is traditionally eaten by hand.
A layered pie of thin pastry with a cheese and herb filling, cut into squares.
Thin pastry, white cheese, eggs, parsley, butter
Boereg is baked by Armenians around the world, especially in Western Armenian families.
Lamb or chicken stewed with onion and tomatoes in its own juices until tender.
Lamb or chicken, onion, tomatoes, saffron, salt, pepper
Bozartma is an everyday dish; the meat is stewed straight away rather than browned, so it stays juicy.
A thick lamb soup with chickpeas, potatoes and quince or apples. Hearty and slightly sweet.
Lamb, chickpeas, potatoes, quince, onion, tomato paste, herbs
Bozbash is made throughout the South Caucasus, differently in every region — with quince in Yerevan, with peas in Shirak.
A cold dish of yogurt with cucumber, garlic, mint and olive oil.
Yogurt, cucumber, garlic, mint, olive oil, salt
Cacik is thinned with water and eaten like a soup, or served thick with meat.
Young lamb or veal stewed in white wine with tarragon, green sour plums and plenty of herbs. A spring dish.
Lamb or veal, tarragon, green sour plums, white wine, coriander, spring onion, garlic
Chakapuli is linked to Easter, when young herbs, tarragon and unripe sour plums appear — the dish is not made without them.
A thick strained fermented dairy product eaten with herbs and bread.
Chakka is made by straining sour milk in bags, giving something between curd and sour cream.
A cold soup of katyk yogurt and water with cucumbers, radish and herbs.
Katyk yogurt, water, cucumbers, radish, dill, coriander, salt
Chalop is a lifesaver in summer heat, when Uzbekistan can top forty degrees.
Lamb baked in a clay pot with aubergines, potatoes, tomatoes and plenty of herbs.
Lamb, aubergines, potatoes, tomatoes, onion, garlic, coriander, basil
Chanakhi is cooked in individual pots where the vegetables simmer in the meat juices; it is especially loved in Tbilisi.
Beef stewed with tomatoes, onion, garlic and chilli. A simple home dish with a rich, spicy sauce.
Beef, tomatoes, onion, garlic, chilli, coriander, khmeli suneli
Such stews are made all over Georgia, with the meat and spices changing with the season.
Thin fried half-moon pastries with a juicy filling of minced lamb and onion.
Wheat flour, water, lamb, onion, herbs, vegetable oil
Chebureki are the best-known Crimean Tatar dish, loved far beyond Crimea.
A stringy cheese pulled into threads and braided, sold fresh or smoked.
Chechil is pulled by hand in hot water and eaten with beer or in salads.
Thin flatbreads filled with curd cheese and herbs; after cooking they are dipped in hot water, buttered and stacked.
Wheat flour, kefir, curd cheese, spring onion, butter, salt
Chepalgash is baked when a child is born in the family and for holidays.
The stack is cut like a cake.
Chicken in a sour cream and garlic sauce with red pepper — an Adyghe festive dish.
Chicken, sour cream, onion, garlic, wheat flour, red pepper
Chetlibzh is made for weddings and guests; the sauce is thickened with flour and served with pasta.
A chicken soup thickened with beaten eggs and flour and soured with vinegar or lemon juice. Delicate with a light tang.
Chicken, onion, eggs, wheat flour, wine vinegar, coriander
In Georgia chikhirtma is considered the best remedy after a feast.
The eggs go in at the very end so they don't curdle.
Fluffy rice cooked with beans, lentils or herbs, served as a side to meat and fish.
Rice, mung beans or lentils, butter, saffron, salt
Chilov is a simpler form of pilaf in which the rice is cooked together with the additions rather than separately.
Adjarian fried eggs with tomatoes, onion, walnuts and herbs.
Eggs, tomatoes, onion, walnuts, coriander, butter
Chirbuli is a traditional breakfast in Adjara; the walnuts make it filling.
Small meat dumplings served in broth or with sour milk.
Wheat flour, egg, beef or lamb, onion, sour milk
Chuchvara is made by the whole family and frozen in batches for winter.
A thin flatbread filled with meat, curd cheese, pumpkin or greens, brushed with butter.
Wheat flour, water, meat or curd cheese, herbs, butter
Chudu are baked across Dagestan; the filling changes with the season and the flatbreads are stacked.
Nuts threaded on a string, dipped many times in grape juice thickened with flour and then dried, making a sweet "sausage".
Walnuts or hazelnuts, grape juice, wheat flour
Churchkhela is made in autumn after the grape harvest.
People took it on journeys because it keeps well and is very nourishing.
Cornmeal cakes with cheese inside, fried until crisp. The melting cheese makes them soft in the middle.
The Svans mix sulguni into the dough, so chvishtari are richer than ordinary mchadi.
Chicken or vegetables fried with onion and tomatoes, with eggs cracked in at the end.
Chicken, onion, tomatoes, eggs, butter, herbs
Chighirtma is quick and simple, made with chicken, spinach or aubergines.
Spicy balls of fine bulgur with tomato and pepper paste, eaten wrapped in lettuce.
Fine bulgur, pepper paste, tomato paste, onion, herbs, pomegranate molasses
Cig kofte was once made with raw meat; today the meatless version is the one usually sold.
Meat and vegetables layered in a kazan and stewed under a lid in their own juices.
Lamb, potatoes, carrots, aubergines, peppers, tomatoes, cabbage, onion
Dimlama is made in summer when vegetables are plentiful; cabbage leaves on top keep the moisture in.
Pieces of bread crumbled into a rich broth with meat, onion and tomatoes.
Wheat bread, lamb, onion, tomatoes, broth
Dograma is made for celebrations, with the whole family tearing bread and meat by hand.
Stretchy ice cream made with goat's milk, salep and mastic — firm enough to cut with a knife.
Maras is the home of dondurma, and vendors put on whole shows with it for customers.
A thick molasses of boiled-down grape or mulberry juice, eaten with bread and used in sweets.
Doshab is boiled down in autumn in big copper cauldrons with no added sugar.
A soup of sour milk or yogurt with rice and lots of herbs, served hot or cold.
Yogurt, rice, egg, spinach, sorrel, dill, coriander, mint
In summer dovga is drunk cold to refresh, in winter eaten hot.
It is stirred in one direction so the yogurt does not curdle.
Boiled meat with potatoes, onion and garlic sauce, sometimes with dumplings.
Beef or lamb, potatoes, onion, garlic, wheat flour
A dish of Chechnya's mountain areas, where meat and potatoes are the basis of the winter diet.
Tiny lamb dumplings in a clear broth with mint and garlic vinegar.
Wheat flour, egg, lamb, onion, mint, wine vinegar, garlic
A skilled cook makes dushbara so small that more than ten fit on a spoon.
Bulgur pilaf with toasted vermicelli and onion. A fluffy side dish for meat.
Bulgur is one of the oldest grains of the region.
In villages people made it themselves by boiling and drying wheat.
A thick dish of fresh cheese, sour cream and flour cooked until the butter separates.
Fresh Ossetian cheese, sour cream, wheat or corn flour, salt
Dzykka is made by mountain shepherds from fresh cheese and eaten hot by dipping bread into it.
A cold bulgur salad with tomato paste, onion, herbs and lemon juice. A fasting dish.
Bulgur, tomato paste, tomatoes, onion, parsley, lemon juice, vegetable oil
Eetch is made during Lent when meat and dairy are avoided.
It keeps well and tastes better the next day.
A thick cornmeal porridge with plenty of sulguni stirred in until it turns stretchy. Served hot with meat and sauces.
Elarji is stirred long and hard with a wooden paddle — its stretchiness depends on it.
A red lentil soup with bulgur, rice, tomato paste and dried mint.
Red lentils, bulgur, rice, tomato paste, mint, red pepper
The soup is named after Ezo, a young woman from Gaziantep whose life inspired songs.
Frozen thin rice noodles in rosewater syrup, served with lemon juice.
Rice noodles, sugar, rosewater, lemon juice
Shirazi faloodeh is one of the oldest frozen desserts in the world.
A many-layered butter flatbread baked in a tandoor — the base of qurutob.
Fatir is rolled very thin and folded many times with butter between the layers.
Meatballs or chicken in a thick sauce of walnuts and pomegranate molasses.
Chicken or ground beef, walnuts, pomegranate molasses, onion, saffron
The dish is common in southern Azerbaijan and Iran, balancing tart pomegranate and sweetness.
An Ossetian pie with meat. Thin dough, plenty of filling and melted butter on top.
Wheat flour, yeast, kefir, butter, beef, onion, garlic, pepper
For celebrations Ossetian pies are baked in threes, linked to the sun, the earth and water.
A small hole is left in the centre of fydjyn to let steam out so the juices don't run.
A soft nougat with pistachios or almonds, made with tamarisk manna and rosewater.
Sugar, egg whites, manna, rosewater, pistachios or almonds
Gaz is the sweet of Isfahan, dusted with flour so the pieces don't stick together.
Rolls of young cheese in a matsoni and mint sauce, served cold.
Young cheese, matsoni, mint, chilli, salt
A Megrelian dish made from fresh cheese on the day it is produced.
Chicken stewed in a thick sauce of sour cream with onion, garlic and red pepper, served with pasta (millet porridge).
Chicken, sour cream, onion, garlic, wheat flour, red pepper
Gedlibzhe is a Kabardian festive dish; the sauce is thickened with flour toasted in butter.
A whole pumpkin stuffed with rice, dried fruit, nuts and honey and baked. Served cut into wedges.
Pumpkin, rice, dried apricots, raisins, prunes, walnuts, honey, butter, cinnamon
Ghapama is a winter holiday dish — there is even a folk song about it, "Hey Ghapama".
Stewed meat with lots of fried herbs, kidney beans and dried lime.
Lamb or beef, parsley, coriander, fenugreek, spring onion, kidney beans, dried lime
Ghormeh sabzi is often called Iran's favourite stew; it is simmered long until the herbs darken.
Round flaky buns with a spiced filling of flour, butter, fennel and turmeric, savoury or sweet.
Wheat flour, butter, eggs, yeast, fennel, turmeric, salt
Gogal is one of the main Novruz treats, along with shakarbura and pakhlava.
A dense porridge of cornmeal made without salt or butter. It is eaten with sulguni, sauces and meat, much like bread.
Gomi is a staple of western Georgia.
It was once made from millet and, after maize arrived, from cornmeal.
Meat fried in its own fat until golden. This was once how lamb was preserved for winter.
The fried meat was covered in fat and kept in jars.
Today govurma is also cooked as a dish in its own right.
Walnuts caramelised in honey and cut into diamonds. A simple treat with two ingredients.
Gozinaki is an essential New Year sweet in Georgia, laid out on the festive table so the year will be sweet.
A thin flatbread folded around cheese, spinach or potato and cooked on a saj.
Wheat flour, water, white cheese, spinach, butter
Gozleme is rolled and cooked right in front of you, traditionally by village women.
A crescent-shaped pie filled with cheese and boiled eggs. It is baked for Christmas, so in Georgia it is also called Christmas khachapuri.
Wheat flour, yeast, matsoni yogurt, sulguni, Imeretian cheese, boiled eggs
A dish from the Guria region of western Georgia.
The crescent shape is explained in different ways, including a likeness to a horn or the moon.
Thin half-moon pastries filled with meat, pumpkin or greens, cooked on a dry pan.
Wheat flour, lamb or pumpkin, onion, herbs
Gutap is the Turkmen cousin of Azerbaijani qutab.
Triangular pastries filled with Adyghe cheese and baked in the oven.
Wheat flour, kefir, egg, Adyghe cheese, butter
Guubat are baked for tea and holidays; the triangle shape is traditional in Adyghe baking.
A sweet porridge of flour toasted in butter with sugar or honey, turmeric and cinnamon.
Wheat flour, butter, sugar or honey, turmeric, cinnamon
Quymaq is made for new mothers and on cold days, as it is considered very nourishing.
A simple flatbread made with ayran and baked in a pan or oven, served with meat and tea.
Wheat flour, ayran, baking soda, salt
Gyrjyn is the everyday bread of the Karachays and Balkars, often filled with cheese or potato.
Meat dumplings sealed with a braided edge that resembles snake scales, boiled or fried.
Wheat flour, egg, lamb, onion, salt
Gurza is a Baku dish named after a viper because the seam pattern looks like its scales.
A round closed flatbread packed with salty Imeretian cheese. It is the most common kind of khachapuri in Georgia, baked at home almost every day.
Wheat flour, matsoni yogurt, baking soda, Imeretian cheese, butter
Named after the Imereti region of western Georgia.
The dough is often made with matsoni yogurt, which makes it soft and slightly tangy.
Khachapuri made with puff pastry: cheese is folded into a square or envelope and baked until crisp and golden. A popular street snack in Tbilisi.
Puff pastry, sulguni, Imeretian cheese, butter
This version appeared later than the classic ones and took root in city bakeries.
An open boat of yeast dough filled with melted cheese, topped just before serving with a raw egg yolk and a knob of butter. You eat it by tearing off the crust and stirring it into the filling.
Wheat flour, yeast, milk, sulguni, Imeretian cheese, eggs, butter
The dish comes from Adjara on Georgia's Black Sea coast.
Its boat shape is often linked to the region's seafaring life, and the yolk to the sun over the sea.
A thick porridge of wheat and meat beaten smooth, eaten with cinnamon, sugar and butter.
Wheat, turkey or lamb, butter, cinnamon, sugar
Halim is eaten for breakfast in winter and during Ramadan, sold in dedicated halim shops.
Black Sea anchovies dredged in cornmeal and fried in a fan shape in the pan.
Anchovies, cornmeal, wheat flour, vegetable oil, lemon
Hamsi is the symbol of Turkey's Black Sea coast, the subject of songs and jokes.
A thick porridge of whole wheat and chicken or lamb, cooked for hours and beaten until smooth. Served with melted butter.
Hulled wheat, chicken or lamb, butter, salt
Harissa is made for holidays and in memory of 1915, when it was cooked by the defenders of Musa Dagh.
It is one of the most symbolic Armenian dishes.
Stewed lamb on a purée of smoked aubergine with cheese and a creamy sauce.
Lamb, aubergines, milk, butter, wheat flour, cheese, tomatoes
The name means "the sultan liked it"; the dish is linked to Ottoman palace cooking.
Aubergines braised in olive oil and stuffed with onion, garlic and tomatoes, served cold.
Aubergines, onion, garlic, tomatoes, olive oil, parsley
The name means "the imam fainted" — according to legend, from delight at the taste.
A soft young cheese with a mild, salty taste — the base of khachapuri and a starter in its own right.
The cheese is made in Imereti and eaten almost right away; it is not meant for long ageing.
A soft brined cheese from cow's or sheep's milk, eaten fresh and used in pies.
Cow's or sheep's milk, rennet, salt
No Ossetian pie is made without this cheese; in Ossetian it is called iron tsykht.
Sevan trout, baked or grilled over coals with lemon and herbs. Tender white flesh with very few bones.
The endemic trout of Lake Sevan is rare today, so it is raised on farms.
A large round pie of meat and onion baked in hot sand or embers.
Ishlekli is baked by nomads and shepherds right in the desert, buried in hot sand.
Balls of bulgur and meat with a filling of fried mince and nuts inside, boiled or fried.
Bulgur, beef, onion, walnuts, butter, spices
Ishli kufta takes skill: the shell is made thin so it does not burst while cooking.
Thin slices of spit-roasted meat on pide bread, topped with tomato sauce, sizzling butter and yogurt.
Lamb or beef, pide bread, tomato sauce, butter, yogurt
The dish was created in Bursa in the 19th century, and the creator's family still uses the name.
Boiled spinach with matsoni, garlic and herbs. A light side for meat.
In Georgian cooking matsoni is used in sauces and starters to soften spicy dishes.
Patties of ground beef with onion and spices, cooked on the grill.
Ground beef, onion, breadcrumbs, egg, cumin, pepper
Every Turkish city has its own kofte, and Istanbul has eateries serving nothing else.
A refreshing drink of toasted barley flour mixed with ayran.
Jarma was drunk in the heat of haymaking: it quenches thirst and gives energy.
Fried lamb offal with potatoes and onion — the name imitates the sizzle in the pan.
Lamb liver, kidneys, heart, tail fat, potatoes, onion
Jiz-biz is a dish of Baku eateries, cooked quickly and served hot.
Pickled flower buds of bladdernut, a shrub that grows in the Caucasus. Served with onion and oil as a starter with meat.
Bladdernut buds, salt, wine vinegar, onion, vegetable oil
Jonjoli is picked in spring and preserved for the year.
It has a tangy flavour slightly reminiscent of capers.
Chicken pieces marinated in yogurt, lemon and saffron, grilled over coals.
Chicken, yogurt, lemon juice, saffron, onion
Saffron gives joojeh kabab its golden colour; it is often served together with koobideh.
An Ossetian pie with cabbage and cheese. Thin dough, plenty of filling and melted butter on top.
Wheat flour, yeast, kefir, butter, white cabbage, Ossetian cheese
For celebrations Ossetian pies are baked in threes, linked to the sun, the earth and water.
The cabbage pie is especially popular in autumn and winter.
A sweet pastry of rich dough with a filling of flour rubbed with butter and sugar, crumbly inside.
Wheat flour, butter, sugar, eggs, matsoni yogurt, yeast, vanilla
Kada is baked in Georgia for holidays.
Armenians and Azerbaijanis have similar pastries, and recipes vary from family to family.
Armenian cabbage rolls: cabbage leaves stuffed with meat and rice, stewed in tomato sauce.
White cabbage, ground beef, rice, onion, tomato paste, herbs
Cabbage tolma is made in autumn and winter, when there are no grape leaves.
A rich soup of lamb's head and trotters simmered for hours, served with garlic and vinegar.
Lamb's head, lamb trotters, chickpeas, garlic, wine vinegar
Kalla-pacha is eaten early in the morning, like khash, especially in winter.
Fried aubergines split open and stuffed with minced meat, onion and tomatoes.
Aubergines, ground beef, onion, tomatoes, green peppers
The name means "split belly"; it is the meaty sibling of imam bayildi.
An Ossetian pie with potato and cheese. Thin dough, plenty of filling and melted butter on top.
Wheat flour, yeast, kefir, butter, potatoes, Ossetian cheese
For celebrations Ossetian pies are baked in threes, linked to the sun, the earth and water.
The potato filling appeared after potatoes spread across the Caucasus in the 19th century.
A purée of fried aubergines with kashk, fried onion, garlic and mint.
Aubergines, kashk, onion, garlic, dried mint, walnuts
Kashk is a dried fermented dairy product that gives the dish its salty depth.
Tiny dumplings in meat broth — the name means "spoon burek".
Wheat flour, egg, lamb, onion, broth, mint
The dumplings are made so small that several fit on a spoon at once.
Lamb ribs and potatoes fried in a kazan until golden.
Lamb, lamb ribs, potatoes, onion, cumin, cottonseed oil
Kazan kebab is served on a large platter with thinly sliced onion and herbs.
A sausage of horse rib meat and fat in natural casing, boiled or air-dried.
Horse rib meat, horse fat, salt, pepper, garlic
Kazy is the centrepiece of the Kazakh dastarkhan, served sliced into rounds.
Meat and vegetables baked in a clay pot, where the vegetables simmer in the meat juices until very tender.
Lamb, aubergine, potatoes, tomatoes, peppers, onion, herbs
Kchuch is the name of both the dish and the clay pot in which it is cooked.
A soup with knife-cut homemade noodles, meat and vegetables.
Wheat flour, egg, beef, potatoes, carrots, onion
Kesme means "cut"; it is an everyday soup in Kyrgyz homes.
A pie filled with mashed potatoes and Ossetian cheese, from the mountain areas of Georgia and Ossetia.
Wheat flour, kefir, potatoes, Ossetian cheese, butter
Khabizgina is the Georgian name for the Ossetian potato pie; it is baked in Kazbegi and Racha.
An Ossetian pie with beans. Thin dough, plenty of filling and melted butter on top.
Wheat flour, yeast, kefir, butter, red beans, onion
For celebrations Ossetian pies are baked in threes, linked to the sun, the earth and water.
The bean pie is baked on fasting days when meat is not eaten.
A soft halva of flour toasted in butter with sugar or honey and milk.
Wheat flour, butter, sugar or honey, milk
Halvaitar is made for celebrations and for new mothers as a nourishing treat.
Fried triangular pastries filled with Adyghe cheese and onion or potato.
Wheat flour, kefir, Adyghe cheese, spring onion, vegetable oil
Khalyuzh are made for celebrations; the triangle shape helps them fry evenly.
A soup with homemade noodles, beans and small meatballs.
Wheat flour, beans, lamb, onion, herbs
Khamrashi is a winter soup of southern Azerbaijan, with noodles cut by hand very thin.
A roll of thin dough filled with meat, potato or pumpkin and steamed.
Wheat flour, lamb, potatoes, onion, cumin
Khanum is cooked in a manty steamer, then sliced and topped with sauce.
